segments.ECC.1.9-11: The Teacher says nothing is new and people are forgotten
segments.ECC.1.12-15: The Teacher, king in Jerusalem, finds all human work futile
segments.ECC.1.16-18: The Teacher learns that much wisdom brings much sorrow
segments.ECC.2.1-2: The Teacher tests pleasure and finds it futile
segments.ECC.2.3-3: The Teacher tries wine and folly to see what is worthwhile
segments.ECC.2.4-6: The Teacher builds houses, vineyards, gardens and reservoirs
segments.ECC.2.9-10: The Teacher becomes great and denies himself no pleasure
segments.ECC.2.11-11: The Teacher sees that all his work gains nothing
segments.ECC.2.12-12: The Teacher turns to think about wisdom and folly
segments.ECC.2.17-17: The Teacher hates life because all work is futile
segments.ECC.2.24-25: The Teacher says enjoying food and work is from God
segments.ECC.3.4-5: The Teacher lists times to weep, laugh, mourn and dance
segments.ECC.3.18-18: God tests people to show them they are like animals
segments.ECC.3.19-20: Men and animals share the same breath and the same end
segments.ECC.3.21-22: No one knows what comes after death, so enjoy your work
segments.ECC.4.1-1: The Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed
segments.ECC.4.2-3: The Preacher thinks the dead and the unborn are better off
segments.ECC.4.4-4: Work and success come from envy of a neighbor
segments.ECC.4.5-6: A fool does nothing; a quiet handful is better than toil
segments.ECC.4.7-8: A man alone works without end and has no one to enjoy it
segments.ECC.4.9-11: Two people are better than one because they help each other
segments.ECC.4.12-12: Two can resist an attacker, and a cord of three is strong
segments.ECC.4.13-14: A poor wise youth is better than a foolish old king
segments.ECC.4.15-16: People follow the new king, but later people forget him
segments.ECC.5.2-3: The Preacher tells worshipers to speak few words to God
segments.ECC.5.4-5: Worshipers must keep their vows to God quickly
segments.ECC.5.6-7: Worshipers must not excuse a broken vow, but fear God
segments.ECC.5.10-11: Those who love money are never satisfied with it
segments.ECC.5.12-12: A worker sleeps well, but the rich man cannot sleep
segments.ECC.5.13-14: Wealth can be lost, leaving nothing for a man’s son
segments.ECC.5.15-17: A man leaves with nothing and lives in sorrow and anger
segments.ECC.5.18-18: It is good to enjoy work and food in the days God gives
segments.ECC.5.19-20: God gives wealth and joy as a gift to people
segments.ECC.6.1-2: God gives a man riches, but a stranger enjoys them
segments.ECC.6.5-6: The stillborn child has more rest than a man without joy
segments.ECC.6.7-8: People work to eat, yet are never satisfied
segments.ECC.6.9-12: No one knows what is good for people in their short lives
segments.ECC.7.3-4: Sorrow is better than laughter; the wise think of death
segments.ECC.7.5-6: A wise person’s rebuke is better than fools’ songs
segments.ECC.7.7-7: Extortion and bribes harm even a wise man
segments.ECC.7.8-9: Patience is better than pride; anger belongs to fools
segments.ECC.7.10-10: The Teacher warns against longing for the old days
segments.ECC.7.11-12: Wisdom is good and protects the life of its owner
segments.ECC.7.13-13: No one can straighten what God has bent
segments.ECC.7.15-16: The Teacher warns against being too righteous or too wise
segments.ECC.7.17-18: Whoever fears God avoids wickedness and folly
segments.ECC.7.19-20: Wisdom is strong, but no one is always righteous
segments.ECC.7.21-22: The Teacher says not to listen to every word spoken
segments.ECC.7.23-25: The Teacher tests wisdom but cannot fully understand
segments.ECC.7.26-26: The Teacher warns of a woman who is like a snare
segments.ECC.7.27-28: The Teacher finds few upright people among many
segments.ECC.7.29-29: God made people upright, but people seek many schemes
segments.ECC.8.2-4: The Teacher says to obey the king’s command
segments.ECC.8.5-7: A wise heart knows the right time to act
segments.ECC.8.8-9: No one has power over the day of death
segments.ECC.8.10-11: Slow punishment leads people to do more evil
segments.ECC.8.12-13: It will go well for people who fear God
segments.ECC.8.14-15: Life is unfair, so the Teacher commends enjoying life
segments.ECC.8.16-17: No one can fully understand God’s work
segments.ECC.9.1-1: The righteous and wise are in God’s hands
segments.ECC.9.2-2: The same fate comes to the righteous and the wicked
segments.ECC.9.3-3: All people face one fate, and all join the dead
segments.ECC.9.4-5: The living have hope, but the dead know nothing
segments.ECC.9.6-6: The dead no longer share in life under the sun
segments.ECC.9.7-8: People should eat and drink with joy
segments.ECC.9.9-10: People should enjoy life with a wife and work hard
segments.ECC.9.11-12: Time and chance come to all, and bad times come suddenly
segments.ECC.9.13-15: A poor wise man saves a small city but is forgotten
segments.ECC.9.16-16: People despise a poor man’s wisdom and ignore his words
segments.ECC.9.17-18: Wise calm words are heeded; one sinner destroys much good
segments.ECC.10.1-3: A little folly spoils wisdom, and a fool shows his folly
segments.ECC.10.4-4: A calm person stays at his post when a ruler is angry
segments.ECC.10.5-7: The Teacher sees fools in high places and slaves on horses
segments.ECC.10.8-9: Workers can be hurt by digging, quarrying or splitting logs
segments.ECC.10.10-11: Skill brings success, as a dull axe needs more strength
segments.ECC.10.12-12: A wise man’s words are kind, but a fool’s words ruin him
segments.ECC.10.13-14: A fool’s many words begin in folly and end in evil madness
segments.ECC.10.15-15: A fool grows tired and does not know the way to the city
segments.ECC.10.18-19: Laziness ruins a house, and money is the answer to all
segments.ECC.10.20-20: People should not curse the king or the rich, even in secret
segments.ECC.11.1-3: People should give freely, since no one knows what comes
segments.ECC.11.6-6: People should sow morning and evening; success is unknown
segments.ECC.11.7-8: People should rejoice in life, but remember the dark days
segments.ECC.11.9-10: A young man should rejoice, but God will judge his actions
segments.ECC.12.3-3: Strong men stoop and those who watch see dimly
segments.ECC.12.4-4: Doors shut, the mill is quiet, and sounds grow faint
segments.ECC.12.5-5: Man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets
segments.ECC.12.6-7: Before death, the dust returns to earth and spirit to God
segments.ECC.12.8-8: The Teacher says that everything is futile
segments.ECC.12.9-9: The Teacher was wise and taught the people knowledge
segments.ECC.12.10-11: The Teacher wrote true words; wise words are like goads
segments.ECC.12.12-12: The Teacher warns his son that much study is tiring
segments.ECC.12.13-14: People must fear God, for he will judge every deed
